headline: Family in Tangail fears two Bangladeshis executed in Saudi Arabia
summary: A woman's family in Mirzapur is desperate for official confirmation after reports that two Bangladeshis were executed for allegedly violating a mosque's sanctity in Makkah.
details: The Saudi Press Agency reported that two Bangladeshis were executed on Wednesday for alleged "immoral acts" at a mosque in Makkah, violating its sanctity and dignity.
A family from Mirzapur, Tangail, is now consumed by anxiety, fearing their daughter may be one of the executed. She had gone to Saudi Arabia for work nearly four years ago.
The woman's father stated that his daughter had previously told him she was framed and imprisoned following an argument with other women working in Makkah.
The family had lost contact with her for about a year, but she called 15 days ago, claiming she might be released in two months.
Her mother, who has not spoken to her daughter for two weeks, is pleading with the government for official confirmation of her daughter's fate.
Local authorities in Mirzapur, including the Police chief and Upazila administrator, stated they have received no official information yet and are conducting inquiries.
The family is desperate to know if their daughter is alive or dead, and if she has passed away, they want her body returned to Bangladesh.
caption:
Two Bangladeshis were executed in Saudi Arabia for allegedly violating a mosque's sanctity. Now, a family in Tangail is desperate to know if their daughter was one of them.

The Saudi Press Agency reported that two Bangladeshis were executed on Wednesday for alleged "immoral acts" at a mosque in Makkah, violating its sanctity and dignity.

A family from Mirzapur, Tangail, is now consumed by anxiety, fearing their daughter may be one of the executed. She had gone to Saudi Arabia for work nearly four years ago.

The woman's father stated that his daughter had previously told him she was framed and imprisoned following an argument with other women working in Makkah.

The family had lost contact with her for about a year, but she called 15 days ago, claiming she might be released in two months.

Her mother, who has not spoken to her daughter for two weeks, is pleading with the government for official confirmation of her daughter's fate.

Local authorities in Mirzapur, including the Police chief and Upazila administrator, stated they have received no official information yet and are conducting inquiries.

The family is desperate to know if their daughter is alive or dead, and if she has passed away, they want her body returned to Bangladesh.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com

headline_marked: 84 detained as [[drug den uncovered at Additional DIG's house]]
headline: 84 detained as drug den uncovered at Additional DIG's house
summary: The Detective Branch (DB) raided a property in Purbachal rented out by Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir, leading to mass arrests and the officer's removal from post.
details: The Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) conducted a raid on a house in the Vatara area of the capital, which was rented out by Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir.
During the operation, which lasted from Monday night until Tuesday afternoon, police recovered a large quantity of narcotics and detained 84 people.
Among those detained, 26 are women. Police reported that people of various ages visited the house to consume drugs.

Following the incident, Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir, who was worked in the Repair and Maintenance branch of the Police Headquarters, has been 'closed' (removed from his post) by an order signed by IGP Mo. Ali Hossain Fakir.
The officer had reportedly rented out the property via online platforms.
The raid uncovered what authorities describe as a drug den where illegal 'DJ parties' were allegedly taking place.
caption:
A senior police officer's rented property was turned into a drug den. 84 people were arrested in a massive raid.

The Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) conducted a raid on a house in the Vatara area of the capital, which was rented out by Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir.

During the operation, which lasted from Monday night until Tuesday afternoon, police recovered a large quantity of narcotics and detained 84 people.

Among those detained, 26 are women. Police reported that people of various ages visited the house to consume drugs.

Following the incident, Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir, who was worked in the Repair and Maintenance branch of the Police Headquarters, has been 'closed' (removed from his post) by an order signed by IGP Mo. Ali Hossain Fakir.

The officer had reportedly rented out the property via online platforms.

The raid uncovered what authorities describe as a drug den where illegal 'DJ parties' were allegedly taking place.

#Bangladesh #PoliceRaid #DrugDen #Dhaka #CrimeNews

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, bdnews24.com, The Daily Star
